title: Maximum Strictly Increasing Cells in a Matrix
summary: Given an m x n matrix with 1-indexed cells, starting from any cell, move to another cell in the same row or column only if its value is strictly greater.
statement: Given an m x n matrix with 1-indexed cells, starting from any cell, move to another cell in the same row or column only if its value is strictly greater. Determine the maximum number of cells that can be visited by repeating this process.
constraints: Move within the same row or column only to a cell with a strictly larger value.
Return the greatest number of visited cells in a valid sequence.
hints: Process cells in ascending value order.
Track the best completed sequence ending in each row and each column.
Compute all cells of one equal-value group before applying their row and column updates.
Every predecessor is smaller and already processed; delayed equal-value updates enforce strictness while row/column maxima capture every legal predecessor.
editorial: Every predecessor is smaller and already processed; delayed equal-value updates enforce strictness while row/column maxima capture every legal predecessor.

tests.explanation: A sequence can move from one to three to four, but not between equal threes, so the maximum is three.
No strictly larger destination exists, so every valid sequence has one cell.
